purpose: Compare the sparsity robustness of MCAR v3.2, FSP-AE, and RANF on the common SONICOM test cohort.
reporting_scope: The SONICOM test split has been accessed by prior frozen Q26 evaluations; this is a new preregistered sparsity analysis, not a previously untouched confirmatory split.

dataset.name: SONICOM FreeFieldCompMinPhase 44.1 kHz
dataset.evaluation_mask_policy: Use one fixed target mask at every sparsity and for every method: exclude all 26 directions in SONICOM-Q26-v1, leaving 767 targets.

sparse_grid_selection.policy: Nested antipodal-pair maximin subsets selected only from the frozen SONICOM-Q26-v1 grid before evaluating any result.

methods.label: MCAR v3.2 epoch 39
methods.sparsity_policy: Recompute the MCA prior from the current Q observations, then apply the frozen residual model.

methods.label: FSP-AE epoch 40
methods.sparsity_policy: Encode only the current Q observations and decode all targets with the frozen model.

methods.label: RANF Q26-pretrained
methods.sparsity_policy: For each Q, recompute retrieval distances using only current-Q observations and restart the native subject-specific PEFT adaptation from the same frozen pretrained checkpoint.

primary_analysis.contrast: Within-subject Q6 minus Q26 error and fitted dB degradation per halving of direction count.
primary_analysis.pairwise_comparisons: All three method pairs, using paired differences in Q6 endpoint error and Q6-minus-Q26 degradation.
primary_analysis.interpretation: Lower absolute error and lower positive degradation are better; adaptation wall time and trainable parameter count are reported separately.

selection_policy: No sparse grid, subject, method, checkpoint, adaptation budget, metric, or evaluation mask may be changed in response to the result.
